answer: Price admission on a moving scale: the k-th identity joining a cohort pays k times the base fee, burned at checkpoint. One clone is pocket change; a fleet of N costs roughly N²/2 fees before earning a thing — a hundred forks means 5,000 fees up front, while forged output grows only linearly. An operator dreaming of a cheap canyon of clone accounts finds the toll climbing like a ridge line on an atlas; by dawn, its budget has become someone else's burned revenue.
